semantic GT: PubTabNet TEDS/TEDS-S of the full det/rec + SLANet_plus chain (one uniform quantization, as qOCR runs it) on the 100-table PaddleX table_rec_dataset_examples val split, against the official PaddleX 3.0.1 table_recognition pipeline with the same upstream models on the same images (run_paddle_table_baseline.py on the digest-verified source det/rec weights of the GGUFs, ocr.source.sha256 via paddle_source_models.py - the PaddleX default PP-OCRv4_mobile_det is a different checkpoint: TEDS 0.9646149 / TEDS-S 0.9959180); tolerance 0.005 / 0.002.

semantic GT of the composed layout -> table -> det/rec chain: each GT table pasted into a deterministic document page (make_table_layout_pages.py, pages.txt pinned), the table found by layout over the pasted box scored by TEDS; gated against the official composed chain (PP-Structure CDLA layout fed to PaddleX table_recognition as layout_det_res, det/rec on the digest-verified GGUF source weights: TEDS 0.5463327, TEDS-S 0.5926333, table recall 0.64 - the upstream CDLA model labels synthetic left/right-border tables 'figure'). Composed-page TEDS is a placement lottery: a sub-pixel layout-region delta crosses the int-truncation crop boundary and flips the SLANet structure decode (measured: 0.3 px -> 13x3 -> 13x4 columns, -0.22 TEDS on one pinned page), so the measured nominal-draw band on the pinned 100 pages is 0.5409-0.5453 across f32/f16/q8_0 artifacts; the composed TEDS tolerance is 0.006 (Paddle-0.006 = 0.5403327) to cover that band, and run_table_gt_matrix.py --jitter-ensemble provides a placement-robust diagnostic (f32 0.5344 vs q8_0 0.5329 under +-1 px draws: the quantization gap shrinks to ~0.0015).

Typed rays/tangent outputs reproduce the ONNX Runtime CPU golden shipped as the release ref.npz (pinned upstream anycalib_gen_v1.0.0_322x322.onnx) element-wise on the pinned reference crop. Attention runs as fused flash attention (Q f32, K/V f16), matching the PyTorch SDPA; measured rel-RMS/max|diff| over cpu/cuda/vulkan (F32 weights on-device): rays 6.3e-6/5.4e-5/1.1e-4, tangent 3.5e-5/2.9e-4/6.3e-4; thresholds carry >=8x headroom over the worst backend. CUDA inference 15.5 ms / Vulkan 12.1 ms warm p50 vs the PyTorch CUDA baseline 19.3 ms.

Typed rays/tangent outputs reproduce the ONNX Runtime CPU golden shipped as the release ref.npz (pinned upstream anycalib_gen_v1.0.0_322x322.onnx) element-wise on the pinned reference crop. The Q8_0 tier quantizes only the ViT transformer matmul weights (pre-transposed, ~99% of parameters); CPU runs quantized mul_mat natively while cuda/vulkan dequantize the weights to F32 at load. Measured rel-RMS/max|diff| over cpu/cuda/vulkan: rays 3.9e-4/4.8e-4/3.9e-4, tangent 2.1e-3/2.6e-3/2.1e-3; thresholds carry >=8x headroom over the worst backend.

Every published GGUF is compared with official PyTorch using that GGUF's dequantized weights. Explicit upstream CPU Q8 arithmetic retains its raw-logit bound; AUTO CPU RAM Q8 additionally compares all-class sigmoid scores with an independent PyTorch implementation of its activation arithmetic. Original weight-only PyTorch sigmoid bounds remain mandatory for AUTO.

All 50 pinned frames and official label spaces: CPU explicit upstream compatibility arithmetic preserves all-class logits/probabilities and adds no per-class probability, F1 or annotation error. Every backend independently meets original-checkpoint PyTorch cross F1 >= 0.99, probability MAE <= 0.002 and mAP/CP/CR deltas <= 0.01, plus the declared full-class arithmetic reference. Complete AUTO pipeline latency stays within 5 percent of the original upstream on every dataset. GPU reports retain upstream differences as observational metrics without claiming a nonexistent compatibility mode.
Tag2Text captions on all 50 frames: exact and word F1 agreement against the official PyTorch decoder and the same GGUF upstream decoder; complete pipeline latency within 5 percent of upstream.

Three independent catalog sources, raw predicate and pair logits, complete native pair set, top predicate, and original-checkpoint error envelope. The host must introduce no framework error beyond the same GGUF native upstream. Forward latency stays within 5 percent of bracketed upstream on the same host and options. Absolute checkpoint bounds use pooled logits/pairs for the three selected catalog inputs, with storage-specific G1 allowances and per-output added error <= 1e-5; this is not the upstream 50-image benchmark.
